pores.name: Pores
tips: Niacinamide helps regulate oil and refine the look of pores over time
A gentle BHA toner 2–3x/week keeps pores from clogging
Daily SPF slows the collagen loss that stretches pores

blackheads.name: Blackheads
tips: Double cleanse in the evening to fully remove sunscreen and oil
A BHA (salicylic acid) toner helps dissolve buildup inside pores
Avoid harsh scrubbing — it can irritate skin without actually clearing pores

texture.name: Texture
tips: A gentle AHA 1–2x/week smooths texture without over-stripping
Layering hydration (hyaluronic acid) plumps and softens rough patches
Consistency matters more than intensity — little and often beats occasional harsh treatments

oiliness.name: Oiliness
tips: Niacinamide helps regulate sebum without over-drying
Don't skip moisturizer — stripped skin often overproduces oil to compensate
A lightweight gel moisturizer keeps oil balanced without heaviness

dryness.name: Dryness
tips: Ceramides help rebuild the skin's natural moisture barrier
Layer hyaluronic acid on damp skin, then seal it in with a moisturizer
Cut back on strong actives (retinol, AHA/BHA) until the barrier recovers

redness.name: Redness
causes: Too many actives layered at once
tips: Centella asiatica (cica) is one of the most consistently soothing ingredients for visible redness
Simplify your routine temporarily while skin recalms
Patch-test new actives on your inner arm before applying to the face

sensitivity.name: Sensitivity
tips: Prioritize a ceramide-rich moisturizer to rebuild the barrier before reintroducing actives
Avoid layering multiple actives (retinol + AHA/BHA) until skin calms down
Look for fragrance-free formulas while your barrier recovers

spots.name: Dark spots
tips: Vitamin C in the morning helps fade spots and protects against new ones forming
Daily SPF is the single most effective way to stop spots from getting darker
Niacinamide can help even out tone alongside a brightening active

acne.name: Active blemishes
causes: Excess oil combined with clogged pores
tips: A BHA (salicylic acid) toner helps clear congestion inside the pore
Benzoyl peroxide spot-treats active, inflamed blemishes
Avoid picking — it prolongs healing and increases the odds of scarring

acneScars.name: Post-acne marks
causes: Slow cell turnover leaving marks visible longer
tips: Niacinamide and vitamin C both help fade lingering discoloration
Gentle, regular exfoliation (AHA) speeds up how fast marks fade
Consistent SPF prevents marks from darkening further in the sun

wrinkles.name: Fine lines & wrinkles
tips: Retinol is the best-studied ingredient for softening the look of fine lines over time
Peptides support skin firmness alongside retinol
Daily SPF is what actually slows new lines from forming

darkCircles.name: Under-eye circles
causes: Thin under-eye skin showing blood vessels
tips: A peptide eye cream can help with puffiness and the look of fine lines
Gently pat products in with your ring finger — never rub the eye area
Sleep and hydration have an outsized visible effect on this area specifically

radiance.name: Radiance
causes: Buildup of dull, dead skin cells
tips: Vitamin C brightens and adds visible glow with consistent use
Gentle exfoliation reveals fresher skin underneath
Radiance responds fast to hydration — don't skip your moisturizer step

faceScanPage.moduleDisclaimer: Use these suggestions as routine guidance. If the skin is painful, swollen or persistently irritated, ask a dermatologist.

pores: Cleanse gently at night so sunscreen and sebum do not sit in the pores.
Use SPF every morning; stretched-looking pores are worsened by sun damage.
Keep exfoliating acids to a planned rhythm instead of using them every day.
blackheads: Remove makeup and SPF fully before bed, then cleanse without scrubbing.
Use a BHA product gradually and pause if the skin feels tight or hot.
Avoid heavy layers on the nose and chin when the area is already congested.
texture: Keep a simple cleanse, moisturize and SPF base before adding strong actives.
Do not scrub texture; use chemical exfoliation slowly and consistently.
Sleep and stress matter here because irritation can make texture look rougher.
oiliness: Cleanse morning and evening, but avoid stripping foams that make skin rebound oily.
Use light layers and wait between products so the routine does not feel greasy.
Drink water through the day; dehydration can make skin feel oily and tight at once.
dryness: Apply moisturizer while the skin is slightly damp after cleansing.
Avoid hot water and long cleansing sessions that remove too much barrier lipid.
Layer hydration first, then seal it with a cream when the skin feels tight.
redness: Keep the routine short while the skin is reactive: cleanser, soothing serum, moisturizer, SPF.
Avoid stacking acids, retinoids and vitamin C on the same irritated evening.
Use lukewarm water and press products in gently instead of rubbing.
sensitivity: Patch test new products for several days before using them all over the face.
Introduce one new active at a time so reactions are easier to understand.
Prioritize barrier repair on recovery nights instead of chasing faster results.
spots: Use broad-spectrum SPF every morning and reapply when outdoors.
Pair brightening actives with patience; visible tone support takes consistent weeks.
Avoid picking marks because inflammation can deepen discoloration.
acne: Cleanse after sweat and remove sunscreen before sleep.
Keep acne actives targeted; more layers can irritate and worsen breakouts.
Change pillowcases often and avoid touching active breakouts during the day.
acneScars: Protect marks from sun every morning; UV keeps post-blemish color visible longer.
Use gentle resurfacing on a schedule, not on already irritated skin.
Do not pick healing blemishes; calm recovery reduces leftover marks.
wrinkles: Use SPF daily; UV exposure is the biggest routine-level factor you can control.
Keep retinoids mostly at night and alternate with recovery nights.
Moisturize consistently so dehydration lines are less visible.
darkCircles: Sleep consistency helps the under-eye area look less tired.
Use a tiny amount of eye product and avoid rubbing the area.
If puffiness is present, try a cool compress for a few minutes in the morning.
radiance: Cleanse at night so dull buildup does not stay under the next routine.
Hydrate before moisturizer; glow often drops when the skin is dehydrated.
Use SPF daily because pigmentation and dullness come back quickly with UV exposure.

niacinamide.name: Niacinamide
niacinamide.summary: Regulates sebum, soothes, strengthens the barrier.

vitamin_e.name: Vitamin E
vitamin_e.summary: Antioxidant, often paired with vitamin C.

spf.name: Sunscreen (SPF)
spf.summary: UV protection — the final morning step.

retinol_aha_bha.headline: High over-exfoliation risk
retinol_aha_bha.reason: Retinol and AHAs both speed up cell turnover: combined the same night, they multiply redness, sensitivity and peeling.
retinol_aha_bha.recommendation: Alternate nights (e.g. retinol Mon/Wed/Fri, AHA the other nights) instead of layering them.

retinol_bha.headline: High over-exfoliation risk
retinol_bha.reason: Same logic as with AHAs: BHA and retinol stack irritation on an already fragile skin barrier.
retinol_bha.recommendation: Give each its own evening, never both at once.

retinol_benzoyl.headline: Benzoyl peroxide deactivates retinol
retinol_benzoyl.reason: Benzoyl peroxide oxidizes retinol and significantly reduces its efficacy, on top of irritating skin if combined.
retinol_benzoyl.recommendation: Use benzoyl peroxide in the morning and keep retinol for the evening, spaced by a few hours — or alternate days.

vitc_retinol_timing.headline: Two powerful actives, two different moments
vitc_retinol_timing.reason: L-AA vitamin C is unstable at a pH close to active retinol; combining them can neutralize part of their efficacy and irritate skin.
vitc_retinol_timing.recommendation: Vitamin C in the morning (antioxidant + protection), retinol at night. Simple, effective, zero conflict.

aha_bha_together.headline: Stacking exfoliants
aha_bha_together.reason: Using two chemical exfoliants the same evening raises the risk of a damaged skin barrier, especially on sensitive skin.
aha_bha_together.recommendation: Pick one per evening, or reserve the combo for very tolerant skin starting at low frequency.

niacinamide_vitc_myth.headline: Myth: this combination is actually safe
niacinamide_vitc_myth.reason: The belief that niacinamide + vitamin C form an ineffective complex comes from old studies at very high temperatures, not representative of a real routine.
niacinamide_vitc_myth.recommendation: You can use them together without issue. If your skin reacts, this combination isn't the cause — look at concentration instead.

peptides_aha.headline: Acidic pH can deactivate some peptides
peptides_aha.reason: Many peptides work best at neutral pH; an acidic exfoliant applied right before can reduce their efficacy.
peptides_aha.recommendation: Apply peptides at another time (morning routine, or a layer after rinsing/neutralizing the pH).

spf_am_only.headline: Retinol increases photosensitivity
spf_am_only.reason: Retinol makes skin more sensitive to UV. Since it's an evening product, the real thing to manage is your SPF the next morning.
spf_am_only.recommendation: No same-evening application to manage — just make sure to apply SPF the morning after a retinol night.

legal.termsIntro: These terms of sale govern the purchase of Haru's paid features: the Premium subscription and one-time face scan credits. Using a paid feature means you accept these terms.
legal.termsServiceText: The free plan includes product scanning, the full product database, and a basic shelf and routine builder. Premium (subscription) adds a full routine audit against your skin profile, unlimited saved products, and unlimited face scans. Without a subscription, face scans can be purchased individually as one-time credits.
legal.termsPriceText: Premium subscription: €6.99 per month. One-time face scan: €9 per scan, no subscription required. Prices are shown in euros on the Upgrade page before payment and include any applicable tax shown at checkout. Haru may change prices for future billing periods; active subscribers are notified before a price change applies to their next renewal.
legal.termsPaymentText: Payments are handled by Stripe, an independent payment processor. Haru does not receive or store your card number; Stripe's own terms and privacy policy apply to the payment step.
legal.termsDurationText: The Premium subscription renews automatically every month until cancelled. You can cancel at any time from the billing portal linked on the Upgrade page. Cancelling stops future renewals; it does not refund the period already paid for, and Premium access continues until that period ends.
legal.termsWithdrawalText: Haru's paid features are digital services made available immediately once purchased. Where the law allows a consumer to expressly waive the standard withdrawal period for this kind of immediate digital service, starting the service (activating Premium or using a purchased scan) is treated as that waiver from the moment of purchase.
legal.termsRefundText: Outside of the above, refund requests are reviewed individually — for example if a paid feature was genuinely unusable due to a technical fault on Haru's side. Contact support with your account email and the date of the charge.
legal.privacyIntro: This policy explains what personal data Haru processes, why, and how you can control it.
legal.privacyDataText: Account details (name, email, password — stored as a hash, never in plain text); your skin profile answers; your saved shelf, personal notes and saved links; your face scan results; your newsletter subscription status if you opt in; and basic first-party usage data used to operate the app, without third-party advertising trackers.
legal.privacyScanText: A photo you submit for a face or product scan is sent to Anthropic's Claude API to generate the analysis and is not stored by Haru — only the resulting result (scores, written notes, summary) is saved to your account so you can consult it later.
legal.privacySubprocessorsTitle: Who else processes data on Haru's behalf
legal.privacySubprocessorsText: Stripe (payment processing), Resend (transactional and newsletter email delivery), Anthropic (photo analysis for scans), and Vercel (application hosting). Each acts as a data processor under its own applicable terms.
legal.privacyRightsText: You can review and edit your account details from your profile at any time, and permanently delete your account and associated data from Account settings. For any other request about your data, use the contact details in the legal notice above.
legal.privacyRetentionText: Account and profile data is kept for as long as your account exists. Deleting your account removes your shelf, notes, saved links, skin profile, scan history and audit history.
legal.cookiesIntro: Haru uses a small number of cookies and locally stored preferences, described below.
legal.cookiesEssentialText: A sign-in session cookie keeps you logged in, and a language preference cookie remembers whether you're using the English or Korean interface. These are required for the site to function and are not part of the accept/reject choice below.
legal.cookiesOptionalText: Your cookie banner choice and your light/dark theme preference are stored locally in your browser, not as tracking cookies. Haru does not currently set any third-party analytics or advertising cookies, regardless of the choice you make in the banner.
legal.responsibilityText: Product sheets, routine guidance, face scan results and all other beauty content on Haru are informational and based on general cosmetic knowledge. They do not constitute medical advice and do not replace a consultation with a dermatologist or another healthcare professional, particularly for persistent, painful or worsening skin conditions.

goodHabits.title: Start with skin logic, then personalize.
goodHabits.subtitle: Haru does not pretend everyone needs the same routine. The base is simple: cleanse, treat carefully, moisturize, protect. Then the details change by skin type.
goodHabits.rulesTitle: Rules Haru uses when checking a routine
goodHabits.disclaimer: Based on dermatologist-style routine basics: gentle cleansing, moisturizing, broad-spectrum SPF 30+, cautious active use, and sunscreen reapplication outdoors. Haru is guidance, not a medical diagnosis.

daily.title: Morning is protection
daily.text: Cleanse only if you wake up oily or sweaty, hydrate, then finish with broad-spectrum SPF 30 or higher every day.

daily.title: Evening is removal and repair
daily.text: Remove sunscreen and makeup, cleanse gently, then use treatment only if your skin tolerates it. Finish with moisturizer.

daily.title: SPF is the non-negotiable step
daily.text: Reapply about every 2 hours when outdoors, and after sweating or swimming. Actives work better when UV is controlled.

daily.title: Do less when skin is irritated
daily.text: Pause retinoids, acids, scrubs and fragrance-heavy extras when skin stings, flakes, burns, or stays red.

routines.am: Gentle rinse or creamy cleanser -> hydrating toner/serum -> ceramide moisturizer -> SPF.
routines.pm: Cleanser -> hydrating serum on damp skin -> richer moisturizer or sleeping mask.
routines.avoid: Avoid foaming cleansers that leave skin squeaky, daily acids, and layering too many actives.

routines.am: Light cleanser -> niacinamide or calming serum -> gel moisturizer -> lightweight SPF.
routines.pm: Cleanser -> BHA 2-4 nights/week or acne treatment -> non-comedogenic moisturizer.
routines.avoid: Do not skip moisturizer; over-stripping often makes oiliness worse.

routines.am: Minimal cleanse -> centella/panthenol serum -> barrier cream -> mineral or gentle SPF.
routines.pm: Cleanser -> soothing serum -> ceramide moisturizer. Add actives one at a time only.
routines.avoid: Avoid starting retinol, vitamin C and exfoliating acids in the same week.

routines.am: Gentle cleanser where needed -> light hydration -> moisturizer only where dry -> SPF.
routines.pm: Cleanser -> treatment by zone: BHA on oily areas, barrier care on dry areas -> moisturizer.
routines.avoid: Do not force one heavy routine on the whole face if your T-zone and cheeks behave differently.

routines.am: Cleanser -> vitamin C or niacinamide -> moisturizer -> SPF.
routines.pm: Cleanser -> gentle AHA 1-3 nights/week or retinoid on alternate nights -> moisturizer.
routines.avoid: Do not exfoliate daily for glow. Irritation creates more uneven tone.
Add only one new product at a time, then wait 1-2 weeks before adding another active.

rules: Apply thinnest textures before thicker creams.
Keep retinoids mostly at night and pair them with morning SPF.
Use exfoliating acids gradually; more tingle is not more result.
Patch test new actives, especially if your skin is reactive.
A routine that you can repeat beats a 12-step routine you abandon.
